paper_title: Black hole superradiance of self-interacting scalar fields
notes: Headline constraint from Fig. 10 (fabounds.pdf in e-print), "Constraints on axion parameter space from black hole spin measurements in X-ray binaries". Plane is (mu [eV], GeV/f), i.e. inverse decay constant 1/f vs boson mass. The paper defines f via lambda == mu^2/f^2 (Eq. 8 quartic self-coupling) and equates f ~ f_a (symmetry-breaking scale) for axion-like particles; reported here as 1/f_a [GeV^-1]. For the QCD axion specifically 1/f = sqrt(0.3)/f_a ~ 0.55/f_a (from lambda ~ 0.3 mu^2/f_a^2, Eq. 5), so a factor <~2 offset from the strict canonical f_a there. Curve = upper boundary (max 1/f excluded) of the UNION of the five per-BH solid-line "high-confidence" spin-down regions (Cyg X-1, GRS 1915+105, M33, GRO J1655-40, LMC X-1), extracted by rasterizing the vector closed paths and taking the per-mass-column top edge; Cyg X-1 dominates the envelope. The excluded region extends down to arbitrarily small 1/f (small self-interaction does not remove the gravitational spin-down bound), so only the upper frontier is physical; the plot bottom (1e-19) is an artifact. This is the m=1 main blob (mu ~ 2.7e-13 to 3.4e-12 eV, peak 1/f ~ 6.3e-13 GeV^-1 at mu ~ 3.1e-12 eV). A separate small m=2 region at higher mass (mu ~ 3.5e-12 to 6.1e-12 eV) sits far lower at 1/f ~ 4e-18 GeV^-1 and is not included in this monotonic curve. New bound derived by this paper (novel superradiance-with-self-interactions analysis of existing X-ray-binary BH spin data; paper states it constrains masses a factor ~2 lighter than prior work). Solid line = "spin-down with high confidence given measured-parameter uncertainties"; paper does not attach a numerical CL to it (the 90% statements in the text concern a separate future-LIGO forecast), so confidence_level=null. Independent of DM density (superradiance does not require a pre-existing abundance).
